 20 Best Things To Do This Weekend In Singapore (20 – 22 Nov 2026)
 Posted on 16 November, 2026 | By Jessica Fang 
 Post Category - Play Play  -  Post Category - Adventures Adventures  -  Post Category - Indoor Indoor  -  Post Category - Outdoor Outdoor Post Category - What's On What's On  -  Post Category - Things to Do With Kids Things to Do With Kids 
 Post Category - Play Play  -  Post Category - Adventures Adventures  -  Post Category - Indoor Indoor  -  Post Category - Outdoor Outdoor Post Category - What's On What's On  -  Post Category - Things to Do With Kids Things to Do With Kids 
 Check out our Weekend Planner for all the exciting things to do this weekend in Singapore (20 – 22 November 2026)! We’ve found plenty of fun events for kids and parents alike, including free ones, so read on to find out what’s on.
 It goes without saying that we’re always looking forward to the weekend! Well, we’re on top of all the best things to do this weekend in Singapore, whether it’s family-friendly events, community happenings or seasonal favourites. Read on for ideas on what to do and where to go, including all the best free things to do in Singapore, kids’ activities , pop-up markets , kids’ theatre shows and more.
 Here’s a snippet of what’s on this weekend (20 – 22 November 2026): There’s a huge school textbook donation drive, and wholesome community events at the National Museum of Singapore and Kampung Admiralty. Christmas events have landed, including the Orchard Road Christmas light-up and Pokémon at Changi Airport and Jewel Changi . Find an array of family-friendly activities at the  Singapore Writers Festival and check out a new exhibition at Children’s Museum Singapore .
 P.S. Looking for more things to do this weekend? Check out our guides to the best  indoor activities , outdoor activities ,  free outdoor playgrounds and free water playgrounds 
 Read more: 101 Best Kids’ Activities In Singapore 
 1. Catch snowfall shows in town (FREE!)
 It’s snowfall season in Singapore -foam snow, that is! There are plenty of places for wintry vibes and it’ll be ongoing through the end of the year. Check them out at our guide to snowfall shows in Singapore , and at a glance below:
 – Changi Airport T3: Now till 3 Jan 2027, 7.30pm & 8.30pm daily, plus 9.30pm on Friday – Sunday
 – Tanglin Mall: Now till 3 Jan 2027, 7.30pm (avalanche) & 7.45pm (snow) daily, plus 8.30 & 8.45 sessions on Saturday – Sunday & PH
 – Great Christmas Village at Ngee Ann City: Now till 3 Jan 2027, 8pm & 9pm daily
 There are also snowfall shows at IKEA Tampines, Suntec City, VivoCity, Capitol Singapore and more! Read all about it here .
 Deets: Now till 3 January 2027, various locations
 2. Donate & pick up preloved textbooks at FairPrice Xtra
 Image credit: FairPrice Group 
 If you’re doing some spring cleaning ahead of the festive season, here’s some good news for those with kids wrapping up the school year. Your old textbooks don’t need to sit at home collecting dust; donate them instead! FairPrice Group’s Share-a-Textbook drive is back. This initiative has been going on for 44 years, and you can give your preloved textbooks a second life. Likewise, you can pick up free used textbooks after the donation drive ends! More info here .
 Donation Drive deets: Now till 28 November, FairPrice Xtra Ang Mo Kio Hub, Changi Business Park, Hougang 1, JEM, Jurong Point, NEX, Parkway Parade, VivoCity & Tzu Chi Humanistic Youth Centre 
 Distribution Drive deets: 4 – 5 December, 9am – 7pm (last session at 6pm), Tzu Chi Humanistic Youth centre 
 3. Avengers-themed trail, carnival & lights at Orchard Road (Free entry!)
 It’s our favourite time of the year to roam the streets of Orchard Road! The Orchard Road Christmas light-up has landed, and there’s lots to do besides admire the lights and decor lining the streets. Check out the Christmas Villages this season; the one at Ngee Ann City has an Avengers:Doomsday themed experiential trail and Christmas tree, plus there’s a Kiztopia carnival with a bouncy castle, carousel and games. Kids can take on workshops at LEGO Santa’s Toy Factory while you’re there, and stay tuned for snow bubble shows that take place daily. More info here .
 Deets: Now till 3 January 2027, 3pm – 10pm (Fridays & Saturdays in December @ 3pm – 10.30pm; Christmas eve @ 3pm – 1am), Ngee Ann City Civic Plaza 
 4. Try wildlife-inspired obstacle courses at the zoo
 Image credit: Mandai Wildlife Group 
 Itching to get moving outdoors this year-end holidays ? The Zoolympix: Stars of Mandai Festive Challenge is back! Take on 10 wildlife challenges inspired by the Mandai Wildlife Reserve’s most iconic residents, ranging from Ah Meng the Orangutan, to Arlo the King Penguin. The course includes everything from balancing to swinging and discovering surprises. Access to the course costs from $15 (Friends of Mandai members can get tickets for $8) – find out more here .
 Deets: Now till 3 January, 10am – 7pm daily, Mandai Wildlife EAST Lawn 
 5. Interactive booths, workshops & more at Grandparents’ Day
 Image credit: National Museum of Singapore 
 Grandma and Grandpa are in the spotlight at Grandparents’ Day at the National Museum of Singapore. That’s right–look forward to an array of intergenerational activities including workshops, interactive booths, talent showcases and more. It’s all with the goal of keeping the family active, staying connected and eating healthy. Admission to the galleries is free for Singapore Citizens and PRs, with general ticket fees for other visitors. There are also plenty of free programmes, with some ticketed workshops. More info here .
 Deets: 21 November, 10am – 7pm, National Museum of Singapore 
 6. Storytelling, yoga & 200+ activities at Singapore Writers Festival 2026
 Image credit: Singapore Writers Festival 
 The Singapore Writers Festival is back with more than 200 programmes, including plenty for younger readers and their families. Inspired by this year’s theme, “Hidden in Plain Sight”, the line-up brings stories to life through storytelling, music, movement, crafts and play. Head to the free SWF Playground in the Living Room at The Arts House for multilingual storytelling in English, Chinese, Malay and Tamil, craft sessions with children’s authors and illustrators, book launches, interactive yoga and lots more. Festival Passes cost $30 ($15 for youths) and include access to 100+ programmes, while selected activities are free. Ticketed programmes start from $5, with many being SG Culture Pass-eligible! More info here .
 Deets: 13 – 22 November, various timings, The Arts House at the Old Parliament, Victoria Theatre & Victoria Concert Hall, Asian Civilisations Museum, Singapore River & Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre 
 7. Mascots, games & more at Our Climate-Ready Home (FREE!)
 Image credit: MSE 
 Haze , heatwaves, harsher storms … the list of worries about climate change goes on. Find out how Singapore is preparing for it at Our Climate-Ready Home , a free family-friendly exhibition with interactive displays, games and live storytelling. Kids can learn about rising temperatures, heavier rainfall and rising sea levels, while meeting familiar mascots including Captain Green, Water Wally and Water Sally. More info here .
 Deets: 18 – 22 November @ Kampung Admiralty 
 8. Check out META’s new AI agent at New Bahru (FREE!)
 Image credit: META 
 Got a long year-end to-do list? Meta’s Hello Muse is taking over New Bahru for a weekend of interactive experiences showing how its personal AI agent can help with everything from planning year-end holidays and finding Christmas gifts to organising CNY reunion dinners . Look out for a giant Muse installation, and explore immersive rooms where you can try planning your next vacation or workout. You can also customise your own Muse and see it projected on the big screen, plus customise your own Muse to take home, while stocks last. There’s free coffee too! More info here .
 Deets: 21 – 22 November, 10am – 6pm, New Bahru 
 9. Shop basics & new collections at UNIQLO’s Thank You Festival
 Image credit: UNIQLO 
 UNIQLO’s Thank You Festival is back this weekend with special deals on everyday LifeWear favourites, including AIRism, HEATTECH and cashmere pieces. Shoppers can also look forward to gifts with purchase, a new Cecilie Bahnsen collaboration, the Monchhichi UTme! collection and exclusive perks for DBS/POSB Cardmembers. More info here .
 Deets: 20 – 26 November, all UNIQLO stores 
 10. Shop Singapore-exclusives at the JISOO pop-up (Free entry!)
 Image credit: Marina Bay Sands 
 Calling all JISOO fans! Marina Bay Sands is bringing the K-pop star’s CLICK era to Singapore with a dedicated pop-up store at The Shoppes. Expect exclusive merchandise, including Singapore-exclusive apparel, plushies, keyrings and JISOO’s POPPOP popcorn line, available for the first time in Singapore. There are also dining deals inspired by her latest release. More info here .
 Deets: From 13 November, The Shoppes at Marina Bay Sands, Digital Light Canvas 
 11. Learn about money at the new Children’s Museum exhibit (FREE!)
 Image credit: Children’s Museum Singapore 
 Children’s Museum has an all-new exhibition, Money Town: Make It Count! and it’s a great way to teach kids aged 5 to 9 all about how to earn, save, spend and donate. Expect lots of hands-on play (there’s even a Money Barn section with aesthetic farm animals for toddlers!). Kids can try their hand at budgeting at the supermarket, investing their cash and even check out currencies used throughout history. Entry is free for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents, and general admission costs $16.35/adult and $10.90/child. Reserve a slot here .
 Deets: 14 November onwards, Tuesday – Sunday, timeslots between 9am & 5.45pm, Children’s Museum Singapore 
 12. Find the Powerpuff Girls & We Bare Bears at Suntec
 If you grew up watching the Powerpuff Girls on Cartoon Network, this one’s a major throwback that you can now share with your kids. Plus, the modern addition of the adorable We Bare Bears! The photo ops and snowfall sessions are free for all, and there are activities such as giant claw machine ball pit, an inflatable playground and floor-is-lava challenge. A minimum spend applies for the activities, but it’s free if you’re a Suntec+ Member! More info here .
 13. Go for a movie date at the vOilah! French Film Festival
 Image credit: vOilah! French Film Festival 
 From 12 to 29 November, you’ll be able to catch 34 French films screening at various locations around Singapore! The vOilah! French Film Festival is back, with festival favourites, classics, dramas, comedies and more animated films on its roster. You can also catch free screenings at selected libraries and community venues. Ticket prices start from $11, with free screenings available too. More info here .
 Deets: 12 – 29 November, various locations in Singapore 
 14. Catch Pokémon meet-and-greets & snowfall at Changi Airport (FREE!)
 P.S.A. Pokémon has taken over Changi Airport and Jewel Changi as part of the PokéXciting event celebrating 30 years of Pokémon! Over at Changi Airport, you can look forward to daily snowfall shows at the Terminal 3 Departure Hall, where you can also snap plenty of pics with the PokéXciting DJ stage. There are also Pokémon meet-and-greet sessions taking place here. Over at Jewel Changi, you can go on a quiz rally and spot all your favourites around the mall. Find out more about PokéXciting! at Changi Airport .
 Meet & Greet deets: 21 & 22 November, 5, 6, 12, 13, 19 & 20 December 2026 at 2pm, 3pm & 6.40pm, Changi Airport Terminal 3 Departure Hall
 PokéXciting: Now till 3 January 2027 (snowfall at 7.30pm & 8.30pm + 9.30pm on weekends) Changi Airport Terminal 3 & Jewel Changi
 15. Check out the new Snoopy pop-up library (FREE!)
 Fans of Snoopy and the Peanuts gang, this one’s for you! There’s a new Snoopy pop-up library at Plaza Singapura, sporting an adorable setup that doubles as fab photo spots. Step into Charlie Brown’s Classroom and strike a pose at the Peanuts School Bus. You’ll also find a Snoopy Garden with reading nooks, and Lucy’s Booth with interactive activities. There are around 10,000 books in physical and digital form, specially curated by the National Library Board. Entry is free, and you’ll need a library-compliant ID card, an NLB eCard or a QR code (request for one with a Singapore-registered mobile number or email here ). And yes, you can borrow books via the NLB Mobile app, too! Look out for meet-and-greet sessions with Snoopy, Charlie and Lucy this weekend!
 Deets: Now till 19 September 2027 (meet-and-greets on 7 – 9 November, 11am, 2pm & 4pm, Plaza Singapura Level 3  
 16. Felines, iconic tunes & more at CATS The Musical
 Image credit: Nardus Engelbrecht 
 CATS, one of the longest-running West End and Broadway shows, lands in Singapore from 29 October to 22 November! Other than seeing the mischievous felines live on stage, you can expect Andrew Lloyd Webber’s iconic score, including hits such as ‘Memory’. Look forward to dance numbers and imaginative costumes at this lively musical in Singapore . Get tickets here .
 Deets: Now till  22 November, Sands Theatre at Marina Bay Sands 
 17. Drama workshop & festive fun at Junior and the Holiday Magic
 Image credit: Singapore Repertory Theatre 
 Christmas has come early, and you can experience it for yourself at the kids’ theatre show , Junior and the Holiday Magic. There’s a musical North Pole adventure to delve right into, plus pre-show drama workshops for children to join. There are drama games, storytelling and imaginative play, featuring the show’s key characters. Tickets for the show cost from $20, with the workshop available as an add-on for $50. More info here .
 Deets: Now till 21 November (show dates); 8 & 15 November (workshop dates), Drama Centre Theatre, National Library 
 18. Ice cream-themed fitness-inspired zones at Sentosa (FREE!)
 Image credit: Sentosa 
 A workout with ice cream as your backdrop? We can’t be more intrigued. Head over to Palawan Beach at Sentosa for HIIT THE BEACH, a free fitness-inspired pop-up featuring some of our favourite ice cream brands from The Magnum Ice Cream Company. Test your speed and agility through eight interactive zones, and check out huge ice cream inflatables and exclusive merchandise. And yes, there are ice cream vending machines around Sentosa to reward yourself for all the hard work! More info here .
 Deets: 24 October – 31 January, Palawan Beach, Sentosa 
 19. Sesame Street Magical Art World Chapter 2
 The Sesame Street Magical Art World is back for Chapter 2, and it will not disappoint fans! This interactive exhibition takes an artsy and immersive spin on our childhood-favourite show, featuring eight zones filled with Sesame Street-inspired artworks. Kids will no doubt love the experience, with plenty of interactive elements built for young visitors. Think: mirrors, shadow play, comic strips, sensory play and more. For the grown-ups, the whimsical aesthetics and throwback elements featuring Elmo, Big Bird, the Cookie Monster and the rest of the gang are enough to make the experience worth the visit! The exhibition is small but mighty, so the 30-minute slot is sufficient to explore the space, too. Entry is free with a minimum spend of $20 on weekdays & $30 on weekends (up to 2 combined same-day receipts). Present your physical receipts at #03-153, capped at 2 pass redemptions per day per visitor, first-come, first-served. Each pass admits up to 2 people.
 Deets: Now till 31 December, 12.30pm – 8pm, Marina Square Level 3 
 20. See Elsa, Woody & more at the Disney Garden of Wonder
 Image credit: Gardens by the Bay 
 The wildly popular Disney Garden of Wonder is back at Floral Fantasy! Spot all your favourite Disney and Pixar characters including Woody, Jessie and Buzz Lightyear from Toy Story 5, Elsa, Anna and Olaf from Frozen, iconic Disney princesses, Mickey Mouse, and Winnie the Pooh and friends–all reimagined in stunning topiary displays. We hear there are also Meet and Greet sessions with Mickey Mouse and Minnie Mouse on select weekends! Tickets cost from $12/adult and $8/child (3 – 12 years old) and you can get them here .
 Deets: Now till 14 March 2027, 10am – 9pm, Floral Fantasy 
 Looking for more fun things to do this weekend in Singapore with kids? Here are more ideas: 
 Watch family-friendly films at Movies by the Beach (FREE!)
 Image credit: Sentosa 
 If you’re looking for free things to do over the weekend, head over to Sentosa to enjoy Movies by the Beach at Palawan Kidz City Roof Garden. Free movie screenings take place every Saturday and Sunday at 7pm. All you have to do is bring your picnic blanket and basket, and good company. No pre-bookings are required, so just show up! You’ll find family-friendly movies including action flicks and comedies on the programme. Find out what’s screening here .
 Deets: Every Saturday & Sunday, 7pm, Palawan Kidz City 
 Head to a Fire Station Open House this weekend (FREE!)
Does your kiddo love fire engines? Did you know you can take them to see a working Fire Station on the weekend for free? Selected Fire Stations are open for visits on Saturday mornings over two time slots – 9am to 9:50am or 10am to 10:50am. Both timeslots are guided tours. Tots will love this experience where they can learn about the cool Emergency Vehicles and their capabilities, watch a demo on donning the full firefighting protective gear, and see how the equipment is used (nothing beats seeing those massive sprays in person!).
 Deets: Saturdays every weekend, 9am to 9:50am or 10am to 10:50am, Selected Fire Stations 
 Borealis Northern Lights at Supertree Grove (FREE!)
 Borealis at Gardens by the Bay is a free immersive light and sound installation at Supertree Grove created by Switzerland-based artist Dan Ache. Using layers of light and cloud particles, the magical splendour of the Northern Lights is recreated. Borealis happens on Mondays and the weekend only (timing below) and is in addition to the Garden Rhapsody light and sound show, where the lights on the Supertrees dance to a changing musical soundtrack that takes place daily at 7.45pm and 8.45pm.
 Deets: Borealis: Mondays, 8pm – 8.30pm; Every Sat & Sun 9pm – 9.30pm, Supertree Grove 
 Read more: 101 Best Activities For Kids In Singapore 
 Cool off at a water playground (FREE!)
 Image credit: Nparks 
 Looking for free things to do this weekend with the kids? Head to one of the many free water playgrounds around Singapore! You’re spoilt for choice–from the animal-themed play space at the free rooftop water playground at Tampines 1 Mall to the ever-popular Far East Organization Children’s Garden with its multiple fountains. There’s also the newly-opened Yew Tee Lifestyle Corridor in the West and Canberra Cove in the North-East!
 Read all about Singapore’s free water play areas .
 Visit a petting zoo or animal farm
 Image credit: Cherilyn Gan – KidzWorld at Singapore Zoo 
 Bring your little animal lovers to interact with animals at petting zoos and animal farms in Singapore . Meet the friendly goats of Hay Dairies, see over 22,000 crocodiles at Long Kuan Hung Crocodile Farm , or do some longkang fishing at Qian Hu Fish Farm . You can also go horse or pony riding at these horse stables in Singapore or simply head to the Singapore Zoo to meet the friendly animals at KidzWorld! It’s a no-brainer when figuring out what to do in Singapore this weekend!
 Read about all the places you can interact with animals in Singapore .
 Explore a park this weekend
 Image credit: Cherilyn Gan 
 Another free thing to do in Singapore over the weekend is exploring one of Singapore’s kid-friendly parks . These parks have free kid-friendly activities , including walking trails and playgrounds. Some new parks that have opened recently include the stroller-friendly Bidadari Par,k which takes inspiration from Winnie the Pooh’s Acre Wood. There’s also the revamped Chinese and Japanese Gardens at Jurong Lake Gardens , where there are 13 different play areas at Forest Ramble and the Clusia Cove water playground .
 Read more about the best parks in Singapore for kids .
 Read more: 101 Best Kids’ Activities In Singapore 
 Go on a cycling excursion (FREE!)
 It’s free (if you have your own bicycle ), it gets the kids away from screens, and it lets you explore nature: cycling makes a great weekend jaunt with the kiddos! There are so many great kid-friendly cycling routes in Singapore , from well-manicured parks to more rugged trails that’ll allow you to truly detox from the daily hustle and bustle.
 Read more about the best cycling routes in Singapore .
 Take the family hiking (FREE!)
 Image credit: Michell Tam 
 Hiking in Singapore is one of our favourite things to do over the weekend with the kids! It’s a great way to not just immerse yourself in nature, but also spot wild animals in their natural habitat. With so many lovely options, you can find hiking trails to suit every difficulty and vibe, including stroller-friendly trails and rugged ones that take you deep into the jungle!
 Read more about the best hiking trails in Singapore .
 Explore a kid-friendly museum this weekend
 Image credit: ArtScience Museum via Instagram 
 Looking for fun things to do this weekend in Singapore to enrich your child’s mind and senses? Bring them to a kid-friendly museum or art exhibition . There are plenty of exhibits and museums where the young ones can soak up some culture or learn something new, such as the Children’s Museum Singapore and the Air Force Museum, both of which are free for Singaporeans and PRs. There are also interactive exhibits such as the permanent FutureWorld at ArtScience Museum . Also check out the life-size dinosaur skeletons at the Lee Kong Chian Natural History Museum which is sure to impress dino-loving kiddos, or let your kid embrace their artsy side at the Keppel Art Centre for Education .
 Read more about kid-friendly museums & exhibits in Singapore .
 Fun things to do this weekend: Indoor playground
 Image credit: The Artground 
 Indoor playgrounds are the ultimate fail-proof way to keep your child entertained (and thoroughly tuckered out) over the weekend – especially if you’re looking for an indoor activity for kids . Thankfully, there are so many options to choose from, making it one of the best things to do with kids ! Bring the kids to zoom around colourful tracks at VroomTown or explore the aviation-themed Kiztopia Jewel! Adventurous kiddos will have a field day at X-SCAP8’s and Superpark’s obstacle courses, and you can add an educational edge at indoor playgrounds such as KidsSTOP at Science Centre Singapore and The Artground.
 Read more about the best indoor playgrounds in Singapore .
 Run around at an outdoor playground (FREE!)
 Image credit: Aisyah Amin 
 There are so many things we love about bringing the kiddos to an outdoor playground ! Firstly, it’s the perfect solution if you’re looking for free things to do with kids ; secondly, the little ones simply thrive outdoors and get plenty of fresh air. Needless to say, you probably have your go-to outdoor playgrounds near you , but check out some of the newer ones that’ve opened: Bidadari Park’s nest-themed playground, Boon Lay Glade’s fire station-themed playground and Tampines Boulevard Park (West)’s small playground with a sand pit.
 Read more about the best outdoor playgrounds in Singapore .
 Beaches, theme parks & more at Sentosa
 Image credit: Sentosa 
 Sentosa Island is packed with plenty of family fun, making it a great choice when wondering what to do in Singapore this weekend! It’s home to some of Singapore’s best beaches and beach clubs , as well as fail-proof kids’ activities in Singapore such as Universal Studios Singapore , The Palawan @ Sentosa where you’ll find the inflatable water park HydroDash , and the hands-on KidZania .
 Read more about all the best things to do in Sentosa .
 Storytelling & programmes at public libraries (FREE!)
 Image credit: National Library Board via Facebook 
 Singapore’s public libraries are wonderfully equipped with plenty of kids’ books and magazines to entertain kids of all ages. We love that this is one of the best free things to do with kids , and a great rainy day activity  These libraries in Singapore have the best kids’ facilities, including kids reading corners, colourful and vibrant decor, educational corners and more! You can also find free storytelling sessions at your nearest public library. If you’re looking for more free things to do this weekend in Singapore, check out their lineup of events here .
 Read more about kid-friendly public libraries in Singapore .
 Things to do this weekend in Singapore: Go cafe-hopping
 Wondering what to do this weekend in Singapore with kids? There are so many kid-friendly restaurants and cafes in Singapore that you can make a day of it! Spend the morning at a cafe with playgrounds and kids’ corners, or bring the kids for a treat of ice cream or cakes and pastries at a dessert cafe in Singapore . Keep your eyes peeled for kids eat free deals as well!
 Bring the kids for a buffet or afternoon tea
 Weekends are for spending quality time as a family, and what better way to do that than with a memorable meal? Find a buffet in Singapore to treat the family to a sumptuous lunch or dinner, or book an afternoon tea in Singapore for decadent treats–some too pretty to eat (but will definitely delight the kiddos).

 About Jessica Fang 
 Jessica is the Managing Editor of Sassy Mama Singapore and is a mum of a feisty preschool kid and two goofy floofy cats. She spends her days taking her daughter to see wild chickens at the park, and her nights telling herself “okay, just one last mission” on her PS5 console. She also sometimes sneaks away for a good concert, and is (unsuccessfully) trying to influence her daughter to appreciate rock music in favour of baby shark.
